Reading the plots and reporting in a paper

Source: vignettes/reporting.Rmd
reporting.Rmd

The check belongs in the design section of a matched study, next to the balance table, and it is done before any outcome is looked at. This vignette shows how to read the output and what to write.

library(propsens)
data("lalonde", package = "MatchIt")
matched <- MatchIt::matchit(
  treat ~ age + educ + race + married + nodegree + re74 + re75,
  data = lalonde, distance = "glm", link = "linear.logit", replace = TRUE
)
# An earlier, faster model set and small settings so the vignette builds quickly; use the
# defaults (logistic regression, BART and the GRF probability forest) in a real analysis.
sensitivity <- propensity_sensitivity(
  matched, algorithms = c("logistic_regression", "random_forest", "gradient_boosting"),
  seeds = 1:2, n_trees = 100, bootstrap_samples = 5
)
numbers <- sensitivity$summary$table
value <- function(name) numbers$with_gate[numbers$quantity == name]

Reading the three plots

Patients plot (plot(x, type = "patients")). Each point is a treated patient. Right = the models disagree about where this patient sits among all patients. Up = the models give this patient different kinds of untreated partners. The upper right is what makes a design fragile. A cloud that hugs the bottom left means the design is robust to the choice of model. Colour shows whether the patient’s logistic score is outside the range of the untreated patients’ scores: fragile patients outside the support point to an overlap problem; fragile patients inside the support point to a region with few comparable untreated patients.

Models plot (plot(x, type = "models")). Each row is a model, each panel a balance statistic. If the points of a panel line up, the balance you report does not depend on the model. If they spread out, it does: say so, and show this plot. Hollow points fail the quality gate; your own model has its own colour and is judged on balance only.

Recurrence plot (plot(x, type = "recurrence")). The per-patient pair recurrence behind pair instability (1 minus its mean over treated patients across models), the second, exploratory summary printed under rank disagreement. Values near the floor (1 / number of models) are common when untreated patients are dense; report pair instability next to rank disagreement, not alone.

What to write in Methods

We assessed sensitivity of the matched design to the propensity model with the propsens package: logistic regression, Bayesian additive regression trees and a generalized random forest (fixed settings, 5-fold cross-fitted scores; seven models in all) were each used for 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching with replacement; we report the mean rank disagreement with the bootstrap rank instability of the logistic model, the balance spread across models and, as descriptions, pair instability and the control spread, all computed without outcomes.

What to write in Results

The numbers below come from the run above, not typed by hand:

Mean rank disagreement was 0.029 (study level); the bootstrap rank instability of the logistic model was 0.036. Exploratory summaries: pair instability 0.524 and a between/within ratio of 4.5. As a description only, 59 % of treated patients received untreated partners that differed by more than one typical match distance across models. The maximum standardized mean difference (including squares and interactions) ranged from 0.23 to 0.24 across models (Figure S1).

If the quality gate left fewer than two models, add: “Fewer than two propensity models met the pre-specified quality criteria (log-loss within 5 % of the best model’s; maximum standardized mean difference on main terms at most 0.10 above the best model’s and at most 0.25), so all models were used.” With balance_rule = "absolute", describe that rule instead; print() states the rule in effect.

When the result says “fragile”

  1. Show the models plot (balance by model).
  2. Choose the design by balance, never by the outcome.
  3. Report the range of the estimates across the models in a supplement.
  4. Look at the treated patients with high control spread: do they share a region of the covariates with few untreated patients? Say so in the Discussion.

What the check does not do

It does not detect unmeasured confounding, it does not fix a fragile design, and it does not tell you which model is right. When logistic regression is correct, the tree models can still disagree with it: the check flags that the choice matters, not which choice is correct. It covers 1:1 nearest-neighbour matching for the ATT only.
